To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human phd2 gene contains two promoters, one of which contains a hypoxia-responsive cis-regulatory element and that PHD2 itself may be a limiting factor in the hypoxic signalling pathway.
PHD2, the main oxygen sensor, is a direct HIFI target gene and is up-regulated during hypoxia.
PHD2 itself, the oxygen-dependent HIF-alpha-degradation enzyme, is regulated by HIF-1 in hypoxia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the proly hydroxylase 2 (phD2) gene.
the regulation of the PHD2 gene.
the molecular mechanisms of oxygen sensing in mammalian cells, in particular with the regulation of PHD2, which is a key player in the oxygen-sensing pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PHD2 protein, which is a prolyl hydroxylation enzyme that targets HIF-1 and HIF-2 for degradation in the presence of oxygen, is a target of the transcription factor HIF-1.
the PHD2 gene is a direct HIFI target gene and that the phd1, phd2, and phd3 genes are regulated by hypoxia via HIF-1.
HIF-1 binds to a hypoxia-responsive site of the phd2/eglin-1 gene and induces phd2/egl-1 gene transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phd gene family is regulated in opposite directions by HIFs and PHDs, respectively.
the PHD enzymes are regulated by hypoxia, which may be an important regulatory mechanism to control the oxygen-dependent degradation of the HIF proteins.
the PHD2 gene is a direct Hif-1 target gene and that the PHD1 gene is not.

the PHD2 promoter is regulated by HIF1, which is a major regulator of the hypoxic response.
